title: kbmon's cleanup panel answers inside its 10-second limit, because backlog.py tidy's plan reads git state with a fixed number of git processes
goal: backlog.py tidy without --apply and kbmon.py --once --panel cleanup each read the state of 30 recorded leftover worktrees and branches with at most 40 git processes, a fixed number however many leftovers there are, so the cleanup panel answers inside its 10-second limit

run:
import os,shutil,subprocess as s,sys,tempfile,pathlib as P
N=30
t=P.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp());c=t/"clone";c.mkdir()
shutil.copytree("_tools",c/"_tools",ignore=shutil.ignore_patterns("__pycache__","test_*"))
shutil.copy("backlog.json",c/"backlog.json")
(c/"kb/_self/backlog").mkdir(parents=True);(c/"kb/_self/backlog/.keep").write_text("")
def g(*a):return s.run(["git",*a],cwd=c,check=True,capture_output=True)
g("init","-q","-b","main");g("config","user.email","a@b.c");g("config","user.name","t");g("add","-A");g("commit","-q","-m","base")
for i in range(N):
    iid="ST-p%07d"%i
    g("worktree","add","-q","-b","work/"+iid,".claude/worktrees/agent-"+iid,"HEAD")
    s.run([sys.executable,"_tools/backlog.py","own",str(c/".claude/worktrees"/("agent-"+iid)),"--class","worktree","--item",iid],cwd=c,capture_output=True,check=True)
d=t/"bin";d.mkdir();log=d/"n";w=d/"git"
w.write_text("#!/bin/sh\necho x >> %s\nexec %s \"$@\"\n"%(log,shutil.which("git")));w.chmod(0o755)
env=dict(os.environ,PATH=str(d)+os.pathsep+os.environ["PATH"])
bad=[]
for name,argv in (("backlog.py tidy",["_tools/backlog.py","tidy"]),("kbmon.py cleanup panel",["_tools/kbmon.py","--once","--panel","cleanup"])):
    log.write_text("")
    p=s.run([sys.executable]+argv,cwd=c,env=env,capture_output=True,text=True)
    n=len(log.read_text().split())
    print(name,"started",n,"git processes for",N,"recorded worktrees and branches (exit",p.returncode,")")
    if p.returncode or n>40:bad.append(name)
sys.exit(1 if bad else 0)

gates.question: How does the tidy plan keep its git reads fixed in number?
options: Batch the commit times and ancestry of all heads and tips in two git reads, check idleness before ancestry and git status, and run git status only for a worktree every other check leaves removable; git cherry stays for a commit the integration main lacks
Replace git cherry by branch --merged for all candidates and keep git status per worktree first

Goal for the worker: plan reads worktree, branch and ancestry state with a fixed number of git processes (one worktree list --porcelain, one for-each-ref, one branch --merged), however many candidates there are. The repro runs this clone's state: it stops failing once the leftovers are tidied (backlog.py tidy --apply) without a fix, so plant 60 recorded worktrees and branches and count git processes (a git wrapper on PATH) for the check that proves the fix.
